transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-12-04 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Jules (Redwood CSM), Priya (NovaEdge Head of ML), Luis (Platform Eng), Hannah (Security Lead), Evan (PM), Marta (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto gen - may be coarse): Sprint-zero orientation, network and security handshake, sample benchmark and prompt set agreement.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick intros? We'll run through goals for sprint zero and then get to network/access items.
[00:14] Priya: Hi all, Priya here, leading ML at NovaEdge. We're excited to get the inference pipeline integrated. Main things for us are predictable latency under 100ms p95 and keeping cost per 1k tokens under target.
[00:26] Luis: Luis, infra. I'll own the VPC peering and firewall rules.
[00:31] Hannah: Hannah from security, I'll manage the compliance checklist and KMS decisions.
[00:36] Evan: Evan, product, mostly here to align on pilot success criteria.
[00:40] Marta: Marta, SRE, I'll help run the bench and monitor.
[00:45] Connor: Connor, Redwood SE. I'll drive the bench and help with model/quant recommendations.
[00:49] Jules: Jules, CSM. I'll run the timeline and make sure we have touchpoints.

[02:05] Maya: Okay, goals: 1) give you access to a staging project, 2) agree on pilot metrics and prompts, 3) run a small perf test with our recommended config. Any other must-haves?
[02:18] Priya: Data residency - some of these prompts will contain EU-only PII, so we need to be clear on where tokens are processed.
[02:27] Hannah: Yeah, plus audit logs. We need an audit trail for all calls for compliance.
[02:33] Maya: Absolutely. For hosted mode we have EU region endpoints; Dedicated gives you more control over residency. We'll include logging and audit detail in the runbook.

[04:10] Connor: Quick technical note — for your use case (short-turn customer messages), we usually recommend a quantized LLM with dynamic batching plus prefix caching. That tends to hit latency SLOs while keeping costs reasonable.
[04:30] Luis: When you say prefix cache, do you mean the KV cache? Sometimes that gets called the K V cache in docs and it confuses folks.
[04:37] Connor: Yep KV cache — key/value. We can send a short doc. There may be some transcription oddities in auto text — sorry if previous notes said K.V cache.

[06:05] Priya: On model choice: we want to compare two variants — a higher-quality 7B and a quantized 13B if that makes sense. Can Redwood host both and route?
[06:15] Connor: Yes, we can host both and set a canary routing to split traffic. For pilot we'd recommend starting 80/20 on the 7B for quality then shift once cost/latency tradeoffs are acceptable.

[07:12] Jules: Timeline check: sprint zero (this week) -> basic connectivity and credentials, next week benchmark run, week after integration with product calls. Sound right?
[07:22] Evan: That matches our internal ship window, yes.

[08:00] Hannah: From security: SSO is non-negotiable for user access. We use SAML. Do you support that in staging?
[08:09] Maya: Yes, we support SAML SSO for staging projects; we'll share the SAML metadata and a checklist to configure. Also discuss KMS — we support customer-managed keys (HSM or cloud KMS).

[09:30] Luis: Networking — do we need VPC peering or can we do VPN? We try to avoid opening public endpoints if possible.
[09:40] Connor: Either works. VPC peering is simpler latency-wise but if you need private on-prem work we can do VPN or private link. For Dedicated deployments peering is typical.

[11:00] Priya: A small Q: what's the token accounting model during bench runs? If we're doing a lot of prompt variants, will that count against free credits or be tracked separately?
[11:10] Maya: We'll label benchmarking runs as test project usage — it'll show in console with token breakdown; we can mark credits as promo if needed. We'll share a spreadsheet template for recording bench results.

[12:45] Marta: On observability — what level of tracing do you provide? We need request->model trace to tie errors to prompts.
[12:52] Connor: We expose per-request traces and model-level latency breakdowns. There's an example agent that captures token-level timing and the runtime path — sometimes the agent mis-transcribes middleware names, that's an auto-gen issue. We'll add a tracing snippet to the runbook.

[14:30] Priya: For the eval set, we plan to send 500 labeled prompts. Is there a preferred schema?
[14:38] Jules: We prefer a CSV with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_category, example_response, notes. Priya: ok will do.

[16:05] Evan: Can you outline what success looks like to close the pilot? Latency, cost, and quality thresholds?
[16:14] Maya: Pilot success criteria (proposal): p95 latency < 120ms for 95% of traffic in staging, cost per 1k tokens under $X (we'll send exact band), and quality pass rate > 88% on the eval set. Those are draft, we can iterate.

[17:45] Hannah: On logging retention, we need 1 year of audit logs for compliance. Does Redwood console support that retention?
[17:53] Maya: Yes, with an add-on retention package. For Dedicated you can export logs to your S3. We'll include options and costs.

[19:20] Luis: Any gotchas re: firewall or NAT gateway rules? We run strict egress.
[19:27] Connor: We'll provide a short whitelist of IP ranges and ports for staging. If you prefer peering, it's easier. Note: some kernel-level optimizations require ephemeral outbound to fetch kernel selection for new models — we'll flag that.

[21:30] Priya: About model rollouts — we sometimes need canaries with quick rollback. Does Redwood support automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if latency spikes?
[21:41] Connor: Yes, routing policies can failover to a compatible model variant or to a lower-cost tier; you can set thresholds and time windows. We'll demo that in the next session.

[23:10] Jules: Operational cadence: weekly 30m sync during sprint zero, then twice weekly for bench runs if needed. Agree?
[23:18] Priya: Weekly works for core team, we may add ad-hoc bench sessions.

[24:55] Marta: For the initial bench, what data should we ingest? We'll need sample traffic patterns and a synthetic workload generator.
[25:04] Connor: We'll share the generator script. Recommend mixing short chatty prompts and longer multi-turn contexts at a 70/30 short/long ratio to mirror production.

[26:40] Evan: Questions about support model post-pilot? If we go Dedicated, what's escalation SLA?
[26:48] Maya: Dedicated includes a 24/7 on-call and targeted SLOs; we'll include the SLA doc. For hosted pilots we have business-hours support plus on-call add-ons.

[28:10] Hannah: KMS detail — we use AWS KMS; can you integrate with customer-managed CMKs? Also, any secrets residency concerns?
[28:18] Connor: Yes, we support AWS CMKs; for private deployments keys never leave your cloud. We'll capture configuration steps in the security checklist.

[30:05] Priya: Any performance expectations for quantized models? We need to set realistic accuracy baselines.
[30:14] Connor: Quantized 13B usually drops ~2–4% on our internal microbenchmarks vs FP16, but throughput/cost gains are material. We'll run both during the bench and provide diff reports.

[31:40] Luis: Are there any preapproved IPs for staging that we can firewall to?
[31:48] Maya: We'll provide a /20 range for staging along with DNS names. If you prefer peering, we'll map subnets.

[33:10] Jules: I'll put deliverables in the calendar and invite the right folks. MVP for sprint zero: staging access, eval prompts uploaded, bench script run and results shared.

[34:25] Priya: One call-out — our legal team asked about data deletion: can you guarantee deletion of PII after pilot?
[34:34] Maya: Yes, for Hosted we have data retention and deletion APIs; for Dedicated you control retention and can rotate keys. We'll include deletion playbook in the runbook doc.

[36:05] Marta: Small nit — we run Chaos testing. Any guardrails to avoid rate-limits during bench?
[36:13] Connor: We'll whitelist your bench run and temporarily bump quotas; also provide a throttle helper to keep you under SLO thresholds.

[37:40] Evan: Are there references or case studies for similar retail/customer messaging flows?
[37:47] Maya: We have a short deck and a couple anonymized case studies; I'll share after the call.

[39:00] Hannah: Security Q: audit of runtime — do you support signed attestations or SOC artifacts to share with our auditors?
[39:08] Jules: We can share SOC2 summary and run an architecture review. If you need extra evidence, we have an enterprise compliance pack.

[40:20] Luis: Small question: will the bench count against tokens for billing? Just want to clarify.
[40:28] Maya: Yes it's tracked as usage; we can label and isolate the project to keep it separate and offer promo credits on request.

[41:50] Priya: Ok, recap and owners?
[41:55] Jules: I'll recap: Connor shares bench script + config (Due 12/09). Jules sends runbook and calendar invites (Due 12/06). Maya shares pricing & docs (Due 12/07). Priya uploads eval prompts (Due 12/08). Hannah completes security questionnaire (Due 12/10).

[43:00] Maya: Anything else?
[43:05] Priya: Nope from me. Thanks, excited to get rolling.
[43:10] Luis: All good.
[43:14] Hannah: Thanks.
[43:20] Maya: Great — we'll follow up in the slack thread with links to the SAML metadata, runbook, and the S3 bucket. Talk soon.
[43:30] (meeting ends)

Notes: Some transcript lines may be mis-attributed or contain minor ASR errors (e.g., product names, kernel selection details). Links referenced during call: runbook (link to be posted), bench script (to be shared by Connor), pricing sheet (to be shared by Maya).
